1.explanation:
1) src/ol/source/XYZ.js: This is the base class for XYZ tile sources and currently has no gutter option or any logic to expand tileSize/tileExtent by a buffer. To support gutter on XYZ you must add a `gutter` option, store it on the source, and—in its tileUrlFunction—apply the same buffer/extent adjustment that TileWMS does.

2) src/ol/source/DataTile.js: Like XYZ this source type also requests tiles by coordinate and has no gutter support. To expose a gutter option on DataTile sources we need to add it to the Options typedef, store it, and apply the buffer when computing tile ranges or when instantiating DataTile so that source tiles include extra pixels to avoid edge artifacts.

3) src/ol/renderer/webgl/TileLayer.js: The WebGL renderer currently doesn’t honor any gutter on sources (it always uploads the full image or the cropped WMS image). We need to update its enqueueTiles/renderFrame logic to tile out only the inner “tileSize – 2 *gutter” portion via adjusted texture coordinates or by clipping in the shader, matching how layer extents are handled, so interpolation won’t sample outside the intended area.

4) src/ol/webgl/TileTexture.js: This class currently crops out the gutter before uploading the texture (`uploadTile_` for ImageTile/ReprojTile), which defeats the purpose of avoiding edge seams. Instead of drawing only the inner pixels into a new canvas, we should upload the full buffered tile and let the renderer draw only the center portion via adjusted UVs. Fixing this file is essential to remove the premature removal of gutter and to support buffered edges correctly under WebGL.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows visible edge-seams (interpolation artifacts) at tile boundaries when rendering XYZ or DataTile sources under WebGL. The current “gutter” (buffer) option only works for TileWMS: other sources ignore it completely. In addition, in the WebGL tile renderer the TileWMS gutter is cropped out before the texture is created, so the interpolation still samples tile edges and you still see seams. The feature request is to allow a gutter/buffer parameter on XYZ and DataTile sources (just like TileWMS) and to change the WebGL pipeline to handle the gutter via geometry or shader (as a layer extent) instead of cropping it away.
